title: compact tool schema v2 and actionable validation hints
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Design and implement a compact JSON schema v2 for tool/function parameters that is backwards-compatible with legacy call shapes, reduces authoring friction, and produces human-actionable validation errors. The goal is to replace parts of the current verbose call-spec surface with a smaller, opinionated DSL that yields better runtime hints, improved telemetry for common failure modes, and an adapter layer for older clients.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Define a compact schema v2 grammar and publish spec draft. 2) Runtime validator returns structured error codes + short remediation hints for top 5 failure classes. 3) Compatibility adapter converts >=95% of legacy call shapes to v2 without user changes. 4) Add telemetry metrics for validation failure types and example message text. 5) End-to-end tests covering streaming, function-calls, and structured outputs with simulated malformed inputs.
design_decisions: - Use a terse attribute set (type, required, coerce) rather than full JSON Schema to reduce cognitive load. - Provide 'hint' and 'example' fields in schema for runtime user-facing guidance. - Implement validation in two phases: quick syntactic checks in ingest path and deep semantic checks in the execution path to preserve latency SLOs. - Compatibility adapter performs field aliasing, optional coercion (string->number, numeric-string trimming), and preserves original value in telemetry for debugging.
tradeoffs: - Compact DSL reduces expressivity vs full JSON Schema but greatly improves developer ergonomics and clearer errors. - Two-phase validation adds complexity to runtime but avoids tail-latency on common requests. - Adapter heuristics risk silent coercions; therefore coercions are opt-in and logged with high-signal telemetry.
implementation_notes: - Create schema parser library in Rust with a lightweight JSON representation used by the runtime and node SDK. - Expose validation error codes: V01 (missing required), V02 (type-mismatch), V03 (out-of-range), V04 (enum-mismatch), V05 (coercion-failed). - Error objects must include: code, field_path, human_hint (<=140 chars), example_value (if applicable), and docs_link. - Validator must be async-safe for streaming requests; fast-path should only run V01/V02 checks.
example_errors: V01: 'user.query' is required — try providing a non-empty string (example: 'How many units sold last month?')
V02: 'max_tokens' expected integer but received '256.0' (we can coerce string->int if client enables 'coerce_numeric').
V03: 'priority' out of range (allowed 1..5) — received 9. Consider using 5 or omit field to use default.
V04: 'mode' must be one of ["summarize", "extract"] — received 'compress'. If you meant 'summarize' set mode: 'summarize'.
V05: coercion failed for 'start_timestamp' — invalid ISO8601 string; expected '2026-03-10T15:23:00Z'.
backwards_compatibility_plan: - Provide an adapter service (invocation-compat) that maps legacy manifest keys to v2 equivalents and emits a deprecation header. - Offer opt-in 'strict' vs 'lenient' validation flags; default remains lenient for 3 months after rollout. - Publish migration guide and automated codemod for common SDK shapes.
telemetry_and_monitoring: - Expose counters for each error code (V01..V05) with route/model tags. - Capture sample invalid payloads (redacted) for high-frequency errors and attach to a dashboard. - Add SLO to limit percent of requests that hit deep-validation to <0.5% of total calls.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for parser and validator. - Integration tests: streaming + function-call flows with malformed param permutations. - Canary rollout on staging with sampling of 1% of production traffic. - Fuzz tests for adapter to ensure no infinite loops when mapping weird key combos.
open_questions: What is the retention policy for captured invalid payload samples?
Do we want to include regex pattern constraints in v2 or reserve for v3?
Should SDKs default coerce_numeric to true or false?
